newsitem.title: USA: De Silguy sees rebound in European economy.
newsitem.headline: De Silguy sees rebound in European economy.

text.p: European Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said on Sunday he expected a rebound in Europe's economy, though this would not be enough to make any early significant reduction in unemployment.

"There are now increasing signs that a moderate recovery to a more healthy pace of expansion may be underway," he said, according to an advance copy of a speech to be given on Sunday to the International Monetary Fund's Interim Committee.
The policy mix had become more balanced, long-term interest rates had declined and consumer and business confidence had stabilised, after falling sharply.

"Together with the prevailing favourable underlying economic fundamentals, these factors are setting the stage for both a near-term rebound in economic activity and for a sustainable medium-term growth process," he said.
But he added, "the expected growth performance is not yet sufficient to secure any visible reduction in unemployment over the near term."
Europe needed to implement labour market reforms to reduce its high levels of unemployment, he said.
He reaffirmed that the European Commission expected growth of two to 2.5 percent next year on average for the European Union as a whole.
He also stressed a need to maintain and reinforce an ongoing shift in the policy mix "in a direction that is more conducive to growth, investment and employment".
"Monetary policy in the Community will have to continue to maintain and achieve price stability while using the available room for supporting other macroeconomic objectives," he said.
